subject: Marketplace listing: Acme Analytics — data localization & automated deletion workback
messages:
From: Sara Liu <sara.liu@acmeanalytics.com>
To: hannah_schmitt@redwood.com
Cc: security@acmeanalytics.com
Date: Mon, 02 Nov 2026 08:12:00 -0700
Subject: Marketplace listing — residency & deletion questions

Hi Hannah,

Thanks for the initial onboarding doc. Before we proceed with the marketplace listing, a couple of residency/retention items came up from our InfoSec and Privacy teams that we need to align on:

- We require that customer-identifiable inference inputs and outputs for EU customers remain resident inside EU regions (no cross-region replication).
- Can Redwood guarantee deletion from all active stores and S3/GCS/Azure blob equivalents within 45 days of a customer deletion request?
- What about backups/snapshots and long-term logs — is there an expected vs guaranteed retention window? Our policy requires that backups be removed within 90 days where possible and that audit logs be retained for 12 months.
- Do any of the marketplace or cloud-managed services used by Redwood (AWS Marketplace listing, GCP Marketplace, Azure Marketplace) introduce forced replication or snapshots we can’t control?

Attached are our security QA notes. Can you confirm per-cloud behavior (AWS/GCP/Azure) and provide a recommended SLA and one-page description we can include in our procurement review?

Appreciate it — Sara

--
Sara Liu
Head of Vendor Security | Acme Analytics

From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>
To: Sara Liu <sara.liu@acmeanalytics.com>
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com, jonas_weber@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 02 Nov 2026 09:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Marketplace listing — residency & deletion questions

Hi Sara — thanks for the clear list. Looping in Ben (sales), Marissa (partner integration), and Jonas (legal/ops) to confirm the specifics. Quick summary from our side:

- We support region-locked hosting for customer inference data in hosted & dedicated modes; for marketplace private offers we can pin listings to EU regions and disable cross-region replication.
- Operational deletion: our standard is removal from active stores within 30 days of a deletion request; full purge from backups and immutable snapshots depends on cloud provider snapshot lifecycles — see below.
- Logs and audit retention can be configured per-customer; default retention is 12 months for audit logs, but shorter windows are possible via contract.

Ben/Marissa/Jonas — can you confirm per-cloud caveats (AWS/GCP/Azure) and whether we can guarantee the 45-day full deletion Acme asked for, including backups? I'll prepare a one-pager once we align.

Thanks,
Hannah

--
Hannah Schmitt
Head of Partner Sales | Redwood Inference

Sara — appreciate the precision. From a go-to-market perspective: pinning to EU regions and a 30–45 day deletion SLA is something we can standardize as a Marketplace addendum for Acme-type customers. Two quick asks for us to move fast:

1) Can Acme accept "best effort" language around third-party cloud snapshots if we document the technical constraints?
2) Please confirm the required deletion window for backups (45 vs 90 days) so we can present a single proposal.

Linking the HubSpot deal (HS-987654321) so we keep procurement notes in the record.

Ben
Senior Account Exec | Redwood Inference

From: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
To: ben_carter@redwood.com, hannah_schmitt@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 02 Nov 2026 11:15:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Marketplace listing — residency & deletion questions

Ben/Hannah/Marissa — quick legal/ops rundown after reviewing Acme_Security_QA.pdf:

- Active data stores: we can contractually commit to deletion within 30 days after a valid customer request. This covers inference inputs/outputs, metadata in our primary stores, and any cached prefixes (we continuously evict stale KV cache per SLO).
- Backups/snapshots: cloud provider managed snapshots (EBS snapshots, GCP persistent disk snapshots, Azure managed disk snapshots) may be retained beyond deletion triggers depending on snapshot lifecycle. We can implement an internal retention policy to attempt removal within 90 days, but cannot absolute-guarantee immediate destruction if a provider enforces a recovery window. Recommend wording: "Redwood will delete customer data from active systems within 30 days and will remove snapshots/backups in accordance with cloud provider capabilities; Redwood will use commercially reasonable efforts to remove such copies within 90 days."
- Cross-region replication: in our Marketplace private offers we can disable cross-region replication for S3/GCS/Azure blob and avoid managed replication services. For certain managed services (e.g., CDN edge caches) we will document TTLs and purging processes.
- Audit logs: we can set configurable retention; default 12 months, configurable down to 90 days per contract.
- Certification note: for EU-residency assurances include references to our SOC2 controls and the architecture diagram (we should attach).

Action items for ops/infra (Marissa/Vanessa): produce a per-cloud matrix showing where data may transiently exist (object store, snapshots, backup vaults, logs) and expected removal windows. I put a proposed clause in the Drive folder.

Jonas
Legal Ops | Redwood Inference

From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>
To: hannah_schmitt@redwood.com, ben_carter@redwood.com, jonas_weber@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 02 Nov 2026 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Marketplace listing — residency & deletion questions

Planning notes / operational constraints:

- Marketplace listing options: for AWS/GCP/Azure marketplace listings we can mark the offering as "EU-only region" and set the default deployment region to eu-west-1 / europe-west1 / westeurope depending on the buyer choice. This prevents Marketplace-driven region selection.
- Backups: our managed backup job runs nightly and writes to encrypted buckets in the same region. For dedicated hosts we offer a retention policy param. For hosted customers on shared infra, we retain backups up to 90 days by default.
- Snapshots & provider-level artifacts: some providers (notably Azure managed disks) create recovery points that can exist outside our direct control for short windows; we'll document these (see attached matrix).
- Proposed attachment: redwood_acme_retention_matrix.xlsx — per-cloud rows showing: primary store location, backup vault location, typical snapshot lifecycle, and recommended contractual retention.

Next steps: I’ll convert the matrix into a one-page customer-facing summary and drop into the Drive link. Suggest we offer Acme: 30 days for active deletion + "commercially reasonable efforts" for backups within 90 days, plus a clause to require notification if provider forces retention beyond our control.

Vanessa Ortiz
Marketplace Ops | Redwood Inference

From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>
To: Sara Liu <sara.liu@acmeanalytics.com>
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com, jonas_weber@redwood.com, vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 03 Nov 2026 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Marketplace listing — residency & deletion questions

Sara — quick update and proposed language for procurement. We reviewed your QA and the team has drafted the following approach:

- Residency: Redwood will deploy and serve Acme EU customer inference data from EU regions only (no cross-region replication by default).
- Active deletion SLA: Redwood will delete data from active systems within 30 days of a valid deletion request.
- Backups/snapshots: Redwood will use commercially reasonable efforts to remove provider-managed snapshots/backups within 90 days and will notify Acme if a provider retains data beyond that window.
- Logs: default retention 12 months, configurable to 90 days via contract.

I attached the per-cloud matrix (redwood_acme_retention_matrix.xlsx) and Acme_Security_QA.pdf back for your reference. If that approach looks good, Ben will proceed with an updated Marketplace addendum and I’ll circulate the one-pager for procurement.

Are you comfortable with the 30/90 split + notification for provider exceptions? If yes, we’ll push the addendum this week.

Thanks,
Hannah

--
Hannah Schmitt
Head of Partner Sales | Redwood Inference
